correctness.rationale: On the nonabelian 2D Lie algebra [e1,e2]=e2 in characteristic !=2, the cyclic commutative cocycle identity for symmetric B is alternating trilinear and hence automatic. Solving B(x◦y,z)=B(y,[x,z]) for symmetric determinant Delta=ac-b²!=0 gives the four explicit products; their commutator recovers the bracket and the anti-pre-Lie identities can be checked on a basis. All bracket-preserving F(e1)=e1+u e2, F(e2)=s e2 reduce forms to c=0 off-diagonal case or c!=0 diagonal square class; isomorphism conditions leave precisely P_infty plus K×/(K×)². Recovering B from a fixed multiplication gives exactly one projective line of forms (scalar fibers). Direct group stabilizer counts produce over odd F_q three product isomorphism classes with orbit sizes q and twice q(q-1)/2, exactly q² fixed-basis products, and 2q-1 unprojectivized form orbits. Independently enumerated ALL nonsingular symmetric matrices and orbits for q=3 (18 forms, 9 products, orbits 3,3,3 and 5 form orbits) and q=5 (100 forms, 25 products, orbits 5,10,10 and 9 form orbits). All-field proof is algebraic, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Liu–Bai 2022 establish construction and two geometric COMPLEX types. Classification over arbitrary fields of ALL 2D nonassociative algebras (Petersson 2000) may already label square-class twists, so no priority is asserted for abstract normal forms alone. The differentiated result is complete cocycle-to-multiplication scalar-fiber map, affine Lie action, quotient of forms vs quotient of products and exact finite-field orbit arithmetic; checked 2004 general count paper gives total algebra classification, not these restricted cocycle-induced counts. Petersson 2000 interior inaccessible: explicit residual risk, not automatic failure because known statements do not imply the restricted orbit census.

value.rationale: The natural nondegenerate commutative-cocycle construction of anti-pre-Lie algebras has a genuine arithmetic descent phenomenon from two complex types to square-class-indexed types. Distinguishing raw cocycle orbits from induced multiplication orbits and calculating their exact stabilizers and counts addresses a motivated quotient/classification problem, not a random finite-field slice.
